newsitem.title: GREECE: Uproar as Greek bank brokerages resume bourse trade.
newsitem.headline: Uproar as Greek bank brokerages resume bourse trade.

text.p: Five brokerages that are subsidiaries of Greek banks began trade on the Athens bourse about 15 minutes before its normal closing time.
This caused uproar as other non-bank brokers were vehemently opposed to the resumption of trading.
The benchmark Athens general share index was up 0.09 percent at 918.91 at 1120 gmt on turnover of 1.71 million drachmas. Reuters screens showed trades in four bank shares only.

One non-bank broker, who asked not to be identified, said "this is ridiculous. The government is putting pressure on them to trade. This will make the existing mess worse. It is a clear move for a cover up," a broker who asked not to be identified told Reuters.
Another broker at Kanaris Securities said the great majority of brokers wanted procedures at the bourse to be tightened up now to prevent the same problems occuring in the future.
He was referring to the crisis which arose last week when brokerage Delta Securities allegedly tried to pay 2.6 billion drachmas in settlement fees to the exchange clearing house with bad cheques.

"Our demand is the improvement of control mechanisms. The great majority of the brokerage community is firmly against the resumption of trade before the present situation is cleared up," the broker said.
Uproar as Greek bank brokerages resume =2

Some brokers said that brokerages Alpha Credit and Ergo Bank were present but not trading. Three brokerages that are subsidiaries of state banks were continuing to trade despite criticism by colleagues.
Others were concerned that the move could be construed as a move to force the exchange to resume trading and cover up a possible scandal surrounding the fraud charges against Delta.

"It is unacceptable that there is trading going on at a time when the exchange's credibility is at stake. I fear that this move may be seen by the investment public as an attempt at a cover up," broker Costas Katsoulis at Katsoulis Securities told Reuters.

With several brokerages said to have been counter-parties to trades with Delta, many where questioning the reason behind the decision to resume trade before the settlement mess was fully investigated.
Several brokers said that if trade resumed, open positions, which could help determine the extent of the Delta fraud, could be closed, making discovery difficult.
